target.name: burning-rate constant K
target.why: an area per time; read so, the rate agrees with initial diameter, extinction diameter and burn time of the same row (see droplets.json)

feature_why.ln_p_kpa: pressure enters droplet burning through gas properties that change slowly with pressure; a logarithm lets one coefficient span 0.7 to 3 atm
feature_why.heptane_x_o2: the two fuels need different amounts of oxygen per unit of fuel, so their response to ambient oxygen may differ
feature_why.heptane_x_co2: a diluent may act differently on a sooting and a non-sooting fuel
feature_why.heptane_x_he: helium raises thermal diffusivity; its effect may differ by fuel

uncertainty.kind: empirical out-of-fold error of the selected family, not a calibrated interval

scope: Methanol and n-heptane droplets in free fall in quiescent O2/N2/CO2/He atmospheres, 0.7 to 3 atm, as in NASA's FLEX table. Not a probability of fire; not for solid materials such as PMMA; not for any gravity but free fall.
